```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(gsDesignNB)
library(ggplot2)
library(lt)
```

## Study specification

The asymptotic power article computes expected information at planned dates.
This study separately evaluates what happens when information and its final
projection are estimated from actual trial data. Each simulated path is evaluated
under fixed bounds and all four recomputed-bound strategies. Primary null
comparisons ignore nonbinding futility; operational comparisons retain it.

Tier A reproduces the eight historical score scenarios under planned nuisance
parameters and two timing constructors. Tier B changes rates, dispersion, and
accrual while keeping the planned design. Tier C evaluates minimum randomized
age, blinded-information targets, and the existing no-adaptation/blinded-SSR
workflows. The target precision is 20,000 null and 5,000 alternative replicates
per cell. Score and Wald comparisons use identical simulated-trial seeds.

Run the workflow and production study explicitly from the source repository:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/gs_strategy_study.R --debug --workers=2
Rscript data-raw/gs_strategy_study.R --production --workers=8 --publish
```

Each cell is checkpointed with its settings, design, raw paths, and summaries.
Additional options select tiers and output directory. Production runs are not
part of vignette rendering or ordinary package tests.

## Available strategy results

```{r strategy-results}
study_path <- system.file("extdata", "gs_strategy_summary.rds", package = "gsDesignNB")
local_paths <- c("../inst/extdata/gs_strategy_summary.rds",
                 "../paper/gs-strategy-results/gs_strategy_summary.rds")
local_paths <- local_paths[file.exists(local_paths)]
if (length(local_paths)) {
  study_path <- local_paths[1]
}
study <- if (nzchar(study_path)) readRDS(study_path) else NULL
```

```{r results, results='asis'}
if (is.null(study)) {
  cat("Production strategy results are not yet bundled. The study specification and existing SSR evidence are available below.\n")
} else {
  cat("Saved study mode: **", study$mode, "**.\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("This saved summary covers **", nrow(study$cells),
      " simulation cells**, generated on ", study$generated_at,
      ". It is not a certificate of completion for the full planned study.\n\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(study$coverage)) {
    print(knitr::kable(study$coverage, row.names = FALSE,
                       caption = "Completed current-source cells versus the full planned study"))
    cat("\nExcluded incompatible or non-production checkpoints: ",
        study$excluded_checkpoints, ".\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  print(knitr::kable(study$cells[c("tier", "scenario", "timing_method", "truth",
                                  "test_type", "cut_rule", "n_sims")],
                     row.names = FALSE, caption = "Coverage of the loaded summary"))
  if (study$mode != "production") {
    cat("These are debug workflow results, not evidence of Type I error calibration.\n\n")
  }
  if (!any(study$cells$truth == "null")) {
    cat("No null cells are included in this summary; these results cannot establish Type I error control.\n\n")
  }
  if (!is.null(study$summary)) {
    selected <- study$summary[study$summary$tier == "A", ]
    selected$failure_rate <- selected$n_failed / selected$n_sims
    groups <- split(selected, interaction(selected$truth, selected$policy,
                    selected$spending, selected$information_estimator, drop = TRUE))
    display <- do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(rows) {
      data.frame(
        Truth = rows$truth[1], Policy = rows$policy[1], Spending = rows$spending[1],
        Estimator = rows$information_estimator[1], Cells = nrow(rows),
        `Rejection range` = sprintf("%.4f to %.4f", min(rows$rejection_rate), max(rows$rejection_rate)),
        `Maximum failure rate` = max(rows$failure_rate),
        `Maximum rejection or failure` = max(rows$rejection_or_failure), check.names = FALSE
      )
    }))
    print(knitr::kable(display, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4,
                       caption = "Tier A results across completed cells only; ranges are not pooled estimates"))
    failed_nulls <- selected[selected$truth == "null" & selected$n_failed > 0, ]
    if (nrow(failed_nulls)) {
      cat("\nSome recomputed-bound null paths fail. Near-nominal rejection alone therefore does not establish error control.\n\n")
      print(knitr::kable(failed_nulls[c("scenario", "timing_method", "spending",
                       "information_estimator", "n_sims", "rejection_rate", "ci_lower",
                       "ci_upper", "n_failed", "rejection_or_failure")],
                        row.names = FALSE, digits = 4,
                        caption = "Null cells with failures, including Monte Carlo intervals and sensitivity"))
    }
  }
}
```

Bound failures and missing-statistic paths remain in the simulation denominator.
They are reported separately, together with rejection-or-failure sensitivity;
they must not be interpreted as evidence of conservative error control. Exact
binomial intervals describe Monte Carlo uncertainty, not uncertainty in the
asymptotic model itself. Production conclusions require checking failure rates
and scenario coverage as well as the rejection intervals.

## Skip near-final interims, retain final follow-up

A separate candidate monitoring policy skips a scheduled interim when the
uncapped spending time, current information divided by blinded projected-final
information, is at least 0.95. This is an information-based decision, not a
decision based on the treatment-effect statistic. The skipped look uses no
additional alpha and does not trigger an efficacy or futility stop. The planned
final date and follow-up requirements are retained; this policy does not promote
the interim to the final analysis. Earlier valid stopping decisions still apply.

At the final look, boundaries use the observed information history from tested
looks and complete the remaining spending. Earlier boundaries and spending are
preserved. The final look is never skipped by the 0.95 rule, and it does not need
a projected-final information estimate. Safety review can continue at a skipped
formal testing look.

For example, one saved trial has current information 57.03 at month 10 and
74.64 at month 18, but projects only 74.33 at the final analysis. The original
implementation rejects the resulting nonincreasing projected information
sequence. This is not an inherently unevaluable month-18 statistic. Under the
revised policy, month 18 is skipped, month 10 retains its original boundary,
and the final analysis remains at month 24.

The source-repository workflow reuses saved trial histories without changing
the active production generator or its fingerprinted monitoring code:

```sh
Rscript data-raw/evaluate_interim_skip.R --self-test
Rscript data-raw/evaluate_interim_skip.R
```

The reanalysis is single-process and resumable. It records actual skipped looks
and trials with a skip, excludes candidates after an earlier stopping decision,
and reports scenario-specific rejection, failure, and final-evaluation counts.
Blinded and unblinded current-information estimators are labeled separately;
both use the blinded projected-final estimate. Adaptive SSR cells are excluded.
Use `--max-sims=100` for a separately labeled smoke test, not calibration
evidence. The full-replication report is written to
`paper/gs-strategy-results/interim-skip/production/summary.md`.

An initial full-replication reanalysis on November 9, 2026 used 20,000 null
trials per fixed-calendar Tier A scenario with unblinded current information:

| Scenario | Trials with an actual skip | Skip rate | Flagged trials remaining |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| High-rate, front-loaded | 17,070 | 85.35% | 248 |
| Low-rate, ramp-up | 40 | 0.20% | 28 |
| Mixed stress | 11,196 | 55.98% | 317 |
| Reference | 7,330 | 36.65% | 716 |

These are sequential skip frequencies, not the larger scheduled-look screening
counts that ignore earlier stopping. The threshold is a candidate operational
rule, not an assurance of Type I error control. Remaining failures and partial
scenario coverage prevent a blanket calibration claim. The original saved study
summary above remains unchanged and describes a different monitoring policy.

## Existing blinded SSR evidence

The completed SSR study covers 90 rate, dispersion, accrual, and treatment-effect
scenarios. Its saved null comparisons include 20,000 futility-ignored trials per
test/dispersion/strategy cell. These use information-driven dates and different
futility calibration, so they are contextual evidence rather than exact
comparators for fixed calendar monitoring.

```{r ssr-evidence}
ssr_path <- system.file("extdata", "ssr_sim_vignette_summary_score.rds", package = "gsDesignNB")
if (!nzchar(ssr_path)) ssr_path <- "../inst/extdata/ssr_sim_vignette_summary_score.rds"
ssr <- readRDS(ssr_path)
nulls <- do.call(rbind, ssr$null_nonbinding_by_test)
nulls$lower <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(nulls)), function(index) {
  binom.test(round(nulls$type1_error[index] * nulls$n_sims[index]),
             nulls$n_sims[index])$conf.int[1]
}, numeric(1))
nulls$upper <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(nulls)), function(index) {
  binom.test(round(nulls$type1_error[index] * nulls$n_sims[index]),
             nulls$n_sims[index])$conf.int[2]
}, numeric(1))
lt::lt(nulls[c("analysis_test", "k_true", "strategy", "n_sims", "type1_error", "lower", "upper")])
```

```{r ssr-plot}
ggplot(nulls, aes(strategy, type1_error, color = analysis_test)) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.1,
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.025, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ k_true, labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Null rejection probability", color = "Test") + theme_minimal()
```

These saved SSR results predate the event-gap consistency fix in
`blinded_ssr()`. New adaptive runs record the corrected implementation and must
not be claimed to reproduce the old adaptive sample sizes exactly. The
no-adaptation comparator is unaffected by that SSR update.
